Over the twelve test years before the trial, the model's top 149 names each year held `r round(early_model$hits_149)` of `r early_model$crossers` crossers and the rule's held `r round(early_rule$hits_149)`. The station can run that rule by hand and get nearly the same names at the top. The model adds the base chance, which sets the size of the gain from contact.

**Contact works, and it pays most close to the band.** In the trial data, `r all_tier$contacted_events` of `r scales::comma(all_tier$contacted_n)` contacted nominees gave in the band the next year, compared with `r all_tier$held_events` of `r all_tier$held_n` held-out nominees. That's a gain of `r round(all_tier$effect, 1)` points, or about `r round(100 / all_tier$effect)` contacts for each added band giver. For nominees who gave $600 to $1,199, it took about `r round(100 / tier_table$effect[tier_table$tier == "$600-1,199"])` contacts. For nominees who gave less than $250, it took about `r round(100 / tier_table$effect[tier_table$tier == "$1-249"])`.

**The first names on the list carry most of the value.** Contacting the top 149 names would add about `r round(list_value$added_by_contact[1])` band givers to the `r round(list_value$band_givers_no_contact[1])` expected without contact. That's about `r round(list_value$contacts_per_added_band_giver[1])` contacts for each one. The next `r list_value$names[2]` names would add about `r round(list_value$added_by_contact[2])` more, at about `r round(list_value$contacts_per_added_band_giver[2])` contacts each. The `r list_value$names[3]` names after those would add about `r round(list_value$added_by_contact[3])`.

**In dollars, the gain is small next to the shortfall.** People who crossed into the band from FY2022 to FY2026 increased their giving by a median of `r scales::dollar(median_increase)`. At that amount, the band givers added by contacting the top 658 names would give about `r scales::dollar(sum(list_value$dollars_at_median_increase[1:2]), accuracy = 1000)` more a year. The whole band gave `r scales::dollar(band_dollars_2026)` in FY2026, and the business problem statement puts the yearly shortfall at about `r scales::dollar(shortfall)`. Treat the dollar figure as an illustration.

**The trial measures the dollars too, and most of them are soft credit.** Contact raised a nominee's giving the next year by about `r scales::dollar(outcome_row("dollars")$effect, accuracy = 1)`, counting each yearly total up to `r cap_text`. Of that, `r scales::dollar(outcome_row("own_dollars")$effect, accuracy = 1)` was the person's own money, and the rest was soft credit. Divided by the band effect, that is about `r scales::dollar(dollars_per_added, accuracy = 10)` for each added band giver. For the top 658 names it comes to about `r scales::dollar(sum(list_value$dollars_measured[1:2]), accuracy = 1000)` in the year after contact, or `r scales::dollar(sum(list_value$own_dollars_measured[1:2]), accuracy = 1000)` in own money. The cap decides this result. Among held-out nominees, `r sum(outcomes$next_total > 25000 & outcomes$contacted == 0)` gave more than $25,000 the next year. With no cap the estimate is `r scales::dollar(outcome_row("dollars_no_cap")$effect, accuracy = 1)`, with a range of `r scales::dollar(outcome_row("dollars_no_cap")$low, accuracy = 1)` to `r scales::dollar(outcome_row("dollars_no_cap")$high, accuracy = 1)`.

**Half of the trial's contacts added almost nothing.** Sorted by predicted gain, the lower half of nominees took `r bottom_gain$contacted_n` contacts and added about `r round(bottom_gain$added_band_givers)` band givers. The top tenth took `r top_gain$contacted_n` contacts and added about `r round(top_gain$added_band_givers)`. At the trial's average gain, 149 contacts add about `r round(149 * all_tier$effect / 100)` band givers. The top 149 names on the list are predicted to add about `r round(list_value$added_by_contact[1])`.

**The gain fades after the first year.** For nominees selected in FY2023 and FY2024, contact added `r round(outcome_row("band_first_year")$effect, 1)` points of band giving the next year and `r round(outcome_row("band_in_two_years")$effect, 1)` points the year after, with a range of `r round(outcome_row("band_in_two_years")$low, 1)` to `r round(outcome_row("band_in_two_years")$high, 1)`. Of the `r nrow(entrants)` contacted nominees who reached the band, `r sum(entrants$band_in_two_years)` were still in it a year later. Count the value above as one year's worth, unless a later trial shows that it lasts.

## Lapsed Donors

```{r lapsed-donors}
# A lapsed person in year t gave in an earlier year and gave nothing in year t - 1
# One row per lapsed person for each year from FY2021, the first year with campaign lists
lapsed_in <- function(t) {
  person_year |>
    filter(fiscal_year < t) |>
    summarise(last_fy = max(fiscal_year), .by = constituent_id) |>
    filter(last_fy < t - 1) |>
    mutate(fiscal_year = t)
}
# A person is on a year's list when a campaign row names them that year with no response; a response is a payment
# Every campaign starts on July 1, so a list gives the year of an appeal and not whether it came before a gift
on_list <- campaign_members |>
  filter(!responded) |>
  distinct(constituent_id, fiscal_year = fy(campaign_start_date))
lapsed <- map(2021:2026, lapsed_in) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(person_year |> select(constituent_id, fiscal_year, total), by = by_year) |>
  left_join(mutate(on_list, on_list = TRUE), by = by_year) |>
  # The list of the year before: the person gave nothing that year, so that list can't follow a gift
  left_join(mutate(on_list, fiscal_year = fiscal_year + 1, on_list_before = TRUE), by = by_year) |>
  # Years in the band up to the last gift
  left_join(giving_history |> select(constituent_id, last_fy = fiscal_year, yrs_band),
            by = c("constituent_id", "last_fy")) |>
  mutate(total = coalesce(total, 0), back = total > 0, band = in_band(total),
         on_list = coalesce(on_list, FALSE), on_list_before = coalesce(on_list_before, FALSE))

# FY2026: lapsed people by the last year they gave, with everyone on the last row
gift_eras <- c("Before FY2010", "FY2010 to FY2018", "FY2019 to FY2022", "FY2023 to FY2024", "All lapsed people")
lapsed_2026 <- filter(lapsed, fiscal_year == 2026)
by_last_gift <- lapsed_2026 |>
  mutate(last_gift = cut(last_fy, c(-Inf, 2009, 2018, 2022, 2024), labels = gift_eras[1:4])) |>
  bind_rows(mutate(lapsed_2026, last_gift = gift_eras[5])) |>
  summarise(people = n(), came_back = sum(back), came_back_pct = 100 * mean(back),
            median_gift = median(total[back]), reached_band = sum(band), .by = last_gift) |>
  arrange(match(last_gift, gift_eras))
kable(by_last_gift, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0), format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      caption = "Lapsed people going into FY2026 by the last year they gave, and how many gave again that year")

# The share of lapsed people who came back, on a list and off it, for two lists: that year's list,
# and the list of the year before (FY2020 has no lists, so that one starts in FY2022)
campaign_checks <- bind_rows(
  "That year's list"            = transmute(lapsed, fiscal_year, back, listed = on_list),
  "The list of the year before" = lapsed |> filter(fiscal_year >= 2022) |> transmute(fiscal_year, back, listed = on_list_before),
  .id = "list") |>
  summarise(on_list_pct = 100 * mean(listed), came_back_pct = 100 * mean(back),
            back_if_on_list = 100 * mean(back[listed]), back_if_off_list = 100 * mean(back[!listed]),
            .by = c(list, fiscal_year))
campaign_checks |>
  mutate(fiscal_year = as.character(fiscal_year)) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Lapsed people by year: the share on a campaign list, and the share who came back on and off it")
# Rows of that table the text quotes
same_year <- filter(campaign_checks, list == "That year's list")
same_year_2026 <- filter(same_year, fiscal_year == 2026)
year_before_2026 <- filter(campaign_checks, list == "The list of the year before", fiscal_year == 2026)

# Everyone who gave in FY2026, and those of them on an FY2026 list
givers_2026 <- filter(person_year, fiscal_year == 2026)
givers_2026_on_list <- semi_join(givers_2026, on_list, by = by_year)
# What the lapsed people on no FY2026 list would give at the average of the lapsed people on a list
off_list_value <- sum(!lapsed_2026$on_list) * mean(lapsed_2026$total[lapsed_2026$on_list])
# Lapsed people who had been in the band before and had missed only one year, FY2021 to FY2026: one row for each
# person and year, so a person who did this twice has two rows. And the same group going into FY2027, one row each:
# they gave in FY2025 and gave nothing in FY2026
skipped_one <- filter(lapsed, yrs_band > 0, last_fy == fiscal_year - 2)
skipped_2026 <- giving_history |>
  filter(fiscal_year == 2025, yrs_band > 0) |>
  anti_join(givers_2026, by = "constituent_id")
# People a test needs in each group to detect a one-point rise in the share who come back
back_rate <- mean(lapsed_2026$back)
test_group <- ceiling(power.prop.test(p1 = back_rate, p2 = back_rate + 0.01, power = 0.8)$n)
```

**Lapsed donors come back at about `r round(100 * back_rate)`% a year, however long ago they last gave.** A lapsed person gave in an earlier year and gave nothing the year before. Going into FY2026 there were `r scales::comma(nrow(lapsed_2026))` of them, and `r scales::comma(sum(lapsed_2026$back))` gave again that year. They gave `r scales::dollar(sum(lapsed_2026$total), accuracy = 1000)` in total, at a median of `r scales::dollar(median(lapsed_2026$total[lapsed_2026$back]))` each. People whose last gift came before FY2010 came back at `r round(by_last_gift$came_back_pct[1], 1)`%, and people who last gave in FY2023 or FY2024 at `r round(by_last_gift$came_back_pct[4], 1)`%.

**Model 1 leaves lapsed people out, because they almost never reach the band.** In FY2026, `r sum(lapsed_2026$band)` of the `r scales::comma(nrow(lapsed_2026))` lapsed people reached it. Of the `r scales::comma(sum(pool$fiscal_year == 2025))` people who gave less than $1,200 in FY2025, `r sum(pool$y[pool$fiscal_year == 2025])` reached it. The trial can't size a contact for lapsed people either, because `r sum(trial$sel_total == 0)` of its `r scales::comma(nrow(trial))` nominations went to someone who gave nothing in the selection year. One small group does better. From FY2021 to FY2026 there were `r nrow(skipped_one)` cases of a lapsed person who had been in the band before and had missed only one year, and in `r sum(skipped_one$band)` of them the person returned to the band. Going into FY2027 that group has `r nrow(skipped_2026)` people.

**The campaign lists can't show that an appeal brings lapsed donors back.** Of the lapsed people on an FY2026 campaign list, `r round(same_year_2026$back_if_on_list, 1)`% gave again that year. Of those on no list, `r round(same_year_2026$back_if_off_list, 1)`% did. That gap shows who is on the lists, not what a list does. The lists name nearly everyone who gave that year: `r scales::comma(nrow(givers_2026_on_list))` of the `r scales::comma(nrow(givers_2026))` people who gave in FY2026, and `r scales::comma(sum(lapsed_2026$back & lapsed_2026$on_list))` of the `r scales::comma(sum(lapsed_2026$back))` lapsed people who came back. From FY2021 to FY2026 the share of lapsed people on a list ranged from `r round(min(same_year$on_list_pct))`% to `r round(max(same_year$on_list_pct))`%, and the share who came back stayed between `r round(min(same_year$came_back_pct), 1)`% and `r round(max(same_year$came_back_pct), 1)`%. The list of the year before is a cleaner test. A lapsed person gave nothing that year, so that list can't follow a gift. In FY2026, lapsed people who had been on the FY2025 list came back at `r round(year_before_2026$back_if_on_list, 1)`%, and those who hadn't at `r round(year_before_2026$back_if_off_list, 1)`%.

**So this data can't put a value on appealing to more lapsed donors.** In FY2026, `r scales::comma(sum(!lapsed_2026$on_list))` lapsed people were on no campaign list. The checks here don't show what an appeal to them would bring. An appeal may still work at the station. Only a test with a random group held out can show it.

## Recommendations

1. **Work the list from the top, and stop when the gain runs out.** Of the top 149 names, `r sum(top_149$level == "$600-1,199")` gave $600 to $1,199. Of those 149, `r sum(top_149$yrs_band > 0)` were in the band in an earlier year. Past the 658th name, each added band giver takes about `r round(list_value$contacts_per_added_band_giver[3])` contacts.
2. **Put former band givers first.** In the trial data, `r former$contacted_events` of `r former$contacted_n` contacted former band givers returned to the band, compared with `r former$held_events` of `r former$held_n` held out. The top 149 names already include `r sum(top_149$yrs_since_band <= 2)` of the `r sum(fy2027$yrs_since_band <= 2)` people who left the band in the last two years.
3. **Use the list alongside officers' own picks.** Among people officers didn't nominate, the model's top 149 names included about `r round(max(not_picked_hits$hits_149))` person who reached the band in each test year. Officers' nominations use information that the giving record doesn't have.
4. **Put current band givers in the next trial.** Over five years, `r sum(band_flow$left)` people left the band and `r sum(band_flow$entered)` entered it. Nobody in the band was in the trial. It doesn't show what contact does for them. A trial of every band giver, split evenly, could detect a 15-point increase in the share who give in the band again within about `r round(stay_trial$years_even_split[stay_trial$rise_points == 15], 1)` years.
5. **Hold out more nominees.** Held-out band givers account for `r round(100 * held_share)`% of the uncertainty about whether contact works better on former band givers. With 94 contacted and 31 held out in each of eight portfolios a year, detecting a fourfold difference would take about `r round(multiplier_trial$more_years[multiplier_trial$ratio_to_detect == 4], 1)` more years.
6. **Skip nominees with almost no predicted gain.** In the trial data, `r bottom_gain$contacted_n` of the `r scales::comma(sum(by_gain$contacted_n))` contacts went to the lower half of nominees by predicted gain, and they added about `r round(bottom_gain$added_band_givers)` band givers. Of the `r who_row("Gave $1 to $249")$contacted_n` contacted nominees who gave less than $250, `r who_row("Gave $1 to $249")$contacted_events` reached the band. Of the `r who_row("Given in 3 or fewer years")$contacted_n` with 3 or fewer giving years, `r who_row("Given in 3 or fewer years")$contacted_events` did.
7. **Decide now which traits the next trial will test.** Age 80 or older, the Alumni constituent type and a second contact in a row might each change the effect of contact. Each rests on 2 or 3 held-out band givers. Writing them down before the station's own records arrive keeps the test honest.
8. **Follow the people contact brings into the band.** Of the `r nrow(entrants)` contacted nominees who reached the band after selection in FY2023 or FY2024, `r sum(entrants$band_in_two_years)` stayed a second year. Holding out some new band givers from further contact would show whether more contact keeps them.
9. **Test an appeal to lapsed donors with a random group held out before counting on it.** About `r round(100 * back_rate, 1)`% of lapsed people come back in a year, and the campaign lists can't show whether an appeal changes that. To detect a rise of one point, a test needs about `r scales::comma(test_group)` lapsed people who get the appeal and as many who don't. Officers can check by hand the `r nrow(skipped_2026)` former band givers who gave in FY2025 and not in FY2026.
10. **Re-estimate every figure on the station's own records before acting.** These data are synthetic, and the data dictionary says the project invented the cultivation and officer tables for teaching.

## Limits

Every Model 2 result rests on `r all_tier$held_events` held-out band givers. The gains on the list apply the trial's odds ratio to people who weren't in the trial, and most of them were never nominated. The base chance ranks people well but miscounts them. With it, the rule predicts `r round(rule_predicts)` band givers among contacted nominees, and `r all_tier$contacted_events` occurred. The right size for the base chance is uncertain too. From FY2023 to FY2025, people who weren't contacted reached the band `r round(sum(trial_level$observed[1:3]) / sum(trial_level$expected[1:3]), 2)` times as often as the earlier years predict, and in FY2026 they matched them. At the earlier rate, the top 149 names would hold about `r round(sum(top_149$p0_earlier))` band givers without contact, not `r round(list_value$band_givers_no_contact[1])`. The trial is too small to show whether contact works better on former band givers. It has no one who was in the band at the time.

# Conclusion

**The model ranks prospects well, and a rule the station can run by hand ranks them about as well.** In the FY2026 forward test, the model's ROC-AUC was `r round(model_2026$roc_auc, 3)`, past the 0.75 target. Its top 149 names included `r round(model_2026$hits_149)` of the `r model_2026$crossers` people who reached the band without contact. The rule that sorts people by giving level and earlier years in the band found `r round(rule_2026$hits_149)` of them too. The model adds the base chance, which sets the size of the gain from contact.

**Officer contact adds band givers.** In the trial data, `r all_tier$contacted_events` of `r scales::comma(all_tier$contacted_n)` contacted nominees gave in the band the next year, compared with `r all_tier$held_events` of `r all_tier$held_n` held-out nominees. That's a gain of `r round(all_tier$effect, 1)` points, or about `r round(100 / all_tier$effect)` contacts for each added band giver. For nominees who gave $600 to $1,199, it took about `r round(100 / tier_table$effect[tier_table$tier == "$600-1,199"])` contacts. Contacting the top 149 names on the FY2027 list would add about `r round(list_value$added_by_contact[1])` band givers.

**The list helps, but it won't close the shortfall alone.** As an illustration, the band givers added by contacting the top 658 names would give about `r scales::dollar(sum(list_value$dollars_at_median_increase[1:2]), accuracy = 1000)` more a year. The business problem statement puts the yearly shortfall at about `r scales::dollar(shortfall)`. Every result about contact rests on `r all_tier$held_events` held-out band givers, and the data are synthetic. The station should re-estimate each figure on its own records before acting on it.

# Historical Notes

The current analysis doesn't support the figures in this section. Don't quote them as results.

**An earlier estimate valued an appeal to lapsed donors at about `r scales::dollar(off_list_value, accuracy = 10000)` a year.** In FY2026, `r scales::comma(sum(!lapsed_2026$on_list))` lapsed people were on no campaign list. The estimate gave each of them the `r scales::dollar(mean(lapsed_2026$total[lapsed_2026$on_list]), accuracy = 0.01)` that a listed lapsed person gave on average. That assumes the lists caused the gifts, and the checks in Lapsed Donors don't support that.
